Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In a directed graph with |V| vertices and |E| edges, the cost of an operation for vertex v equals its out-degree, and we can analyze both the worst case and the amortized average.

* **(a) Worst possible single operation:** The worst case occurs when a single vertex is the source of every edge in the graph, giving it an out-degree of |E|. Therefore, the cost of the worst possible single operation is **|E|** (i.e., O(|E|)).

* **(b) Average amortized cost (aggregate analysis):** The total cost across all |V| operations is the sum of the out-degrees of all vertices, which equals |E| (since each edge contributes exactly 1 to the out-degree of its source). Dividing this total by the number of operations gives the amortized cost of **|E| / |V|** per operation.
